comparison: Both evaluate curtaining and plasma source performance (C14-C22) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval finds converging experimental evidence sufficient. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'significant results' and useful quantitative analyses, but R2 indicates temporal curtaining behavior (C17) needs more data, creating partial disagreement on completeness.

Both address temporal curtaining behavior (C17). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on direct observation of no temporal trends. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, specifically requesting 'description of curtaining over time' and noting insufficient evidence on how different sources behave temporally.

Both evaluate resolution improvement claims (C37-C39, C71-C73). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with visual, quantitative FRC, and geometric evidence. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about explanation for resolution loss at tilted angles, contrast differences on curtain edges, and potential astigmatism effects on comparisons.

Both evaluate optimized imaging parameters (C25-C26) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these are empirically optimized and reproducible though system-specific. Peer reviewers acknowledge useful practical guidance as part of methodological contribution without critique.

Both evaluate HeLa cell prophase observations (C27-C30) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval finds direct measurements align with literature. Peer reviewers accept these as demonstrating technique capabilities across the expected resolution range without specific concerns.

Both evaluate volumetric measurements of subcellular structures (C31-C36) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval finds quantitative measurements specific and internally consistent across scales. Peer reviewers accept these as demonstrating accurate determination of biological ultrastructural arrangements.

Both evaluate synaptic vesicle observations (C43-C46, C68-C69, C95) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval finds direct experimental observations with literature-aligned counts. Peer reviewers acknowledge biological observations and accept novelty claims about visualization scale and rapid volumetric imaging advantages.

Both evaluate MCS measurements in neurons (C47-C49) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides specific counts and volumes but notes limited acquisition volume. Peer reviewers accept these as examples of cellular organization visualization capability without challenge.

Both evaluate cardiac tissue measurements (C50-C54, C96-C97) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval finds good literature agreement and appropriate interpretation of sarcomere length. Peer reviewers accept quantitative measurements as demonstrating technique utility for tissue comparison.

Both evaluate bead-based precision measurements (C40-C42) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval finds quantitative demonstration of system precision and stability. Peer reviewers accept these technical characterization metrics as methodological validation supporting controllability claims.

Both address beam profile measurements (C23-C24). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with direct measurements providing important characterization. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, requesting additional 'data on milling resolution and beam cross-section' to assess impact on z-resolution, finding characterization incomplete.

Both evaluate radiation damage and stability claims (C55-C58, C94) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval finds FRC analysis and dose calculations support claims, though C57 is expectation-based. Peer reviewers accept damage assessments and lack of resolution degradation as supporting technique viability.

Both address segmentation validation (C60-C61, C74-C76). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with Dice scores >0.85 indicating good agreement. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, requesting more extensive automated segmentation application as 'unbiased and practical metric' to prove biological interpretability at scale.

Both evaluate correlative imaging claims (C80-C85). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding successful correlation and appropriate conclusions about workflow compatibility. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting readers will be 'disappointed' and requiring either demonstration of cryo-ET correlation or explicit statement that it's 'currently not possible.'

Both address charging artifacts (C86-C87, C3, C76). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with consistent observations across samples. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, stating paper 'does not show or discuss how plasma beams can mitigate charging artifacts' and requesting comparison with different sources including Gallium before computational correction.

Both evaluate overall capabilities and advantages (C4, C100-C106). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on range of experimental demonstrations. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, calling this 'important work' with 'substantial' results meriting publication, though noting specific applications require further validation.

Both evaluate argon vs nitrogen comparison (C77-C79). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting confounding of cell type with plasma type makes isolating plasma effect difficult. Peer reviewers also rate as UNCERTAIN, requesting more systematic comparison data as this finding appears to contradict main conclusion favoring argon.

Both evaluate contextual and background claims (C1-C13, C62-C67 for OpenEval; C2, C5-C10 for peer). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these are literature-based knowledge claims. Peer reviewers accept problem statement without challenge, acknowledging the field motivation.

OpenEval evaluates timing measurements (C59, C104) as SUPPORTED, identifying SEM as rate-limiting and noting practical throughput. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these timing claims.

OpenEval evaluates general damage considerations (C92-C94) as SUPPORTED, with literature-based claims and observational validation. Peer reviewers address C94 within R11 but do not separately evaluate these general damage claims.

OpenEval evaluates pathology application claims (C98-C99) as UNCERTAIN, noting C99 is speculative without validation on diseased tissue. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses pathology applications.
